correctness.rationale: Phase rotation sends a positive weighted unilateral shift T to e^{iθ}T unitarily, so its numerical radius is the top eigenvalue of compact nonnegative Jacobi J=(T+T*)/2. The exact positive four-periodic ground state φ=(1,r,r,1) with r=(s-t+sqrt((s-t)^2+4))/2 and upper edge L=(r+t)/2 gives a quadratic-form identity with nonnegative gradient, a boundary penalty t v0²/2, and a confining potential. Cell resistance S=2/r+1/(sr²)+1/t, mean mass (1+r²)/2, and the Cauchy equality establish α=4/[(1+r²)S]=2st/[L(s+t)sqrt((s-t)^2+4)]. With ε=-log(q) and h=ε^{1/3}, kinetic and linear confining energy balance at order h². The proof’s compactness/tightness, four-site interpolation, Dirichlet boundary from the positive penalty, weak-liminf and exact resistance-minimizing recovery lead to the half-line operator -α d²/dx²+Lx, whose ground eigenvalue is a_Ai α^{1/3}L^{2/3}. Thus (L-w(T))/(-log q)^{2/3} tends to that exact constant for fixed s,t>0. The bundled exact-rational code verifies the discrete identity and coefficient; independent bounded finite-section behavior was consistent, but neither substitutes for the infinite variational proof.
residual_risks: The asymptotic is pointwise for fixed positive s,t; no uniform error or rate was established.
